title: Exercise 2. Creating vector objects
text:
Objectives

Create new GeoPackage;
Create new tables in existing GeoPackage;
Create vector objects;
modify vector objects;
snapping and tracing;
modify attributes.



Key steps

Create a GeoPackage file;
Create a table in a GeoPackage file;
Create point objects;
Create polyline objects;
Create polygon objects;
Snapping and tracing;
Advanced editing operations:

rings;
parts;
splitting and merging objects;
etc.

(only if there is time left) Feature annotations.



Input data for training
A fragment of the Unified Electronic Cartographic Basemap of Russian Federation (rus. Единая электронная картографическая основа, ЕЭКО, officially transliterated as EEKO).



Screenshots and additional information

Create a new GeoPackage
To create a new GeoPackage, toggle New GeoPackage Layer button on the Data Source Manager toolbar, or select “Layer” – “Create Layer…” – “New GeoPackage layer”, or press Ctrl+Shift+N.

Enter file name, table name, select geometry type and CRS. In the “New field” block, enter a field name and select its type, then press “Add to Fields list”. Repeat for other required fields.


Create a new table in existing GeoPackage
To add a new table into the existing GeoPackage, find it in the Browser panel, then press right mouse button and select “New Table…”

The interface for creating a new table contains the same settings as the interface for creating a new database (GeoPackage), but they are organized in a somewhat different way.

title: Exercise 1. Map Symbolization
text:
Objectives

QGIS interface;
vector symbology;
raster symbology;
map layout.



Key steps

Create a new user profile;
Create a new project;
Add vector data;
Symbolize data;

Single symbols;
Categorized symbols;

Enable labels;
Change map projection;
Create map layout;

Add map;
Fix layers for map;
Add legend;
Add scalebar;
Add author info;

Return to main QGIS window;

Toggle off layers;

Add raster data;
Symbolize raster data;
Create a copy of layout;
Export layouts to external formats.



Screenshots and additional explanations

Creating a new user profile
User profiles allow for quick switching between settings. Create a new profile and switch its language to English. Your default profile will keep your original language.



QGIS interface
Four main elements:

Map frame (now empty)
Toolbars (upper part)
Browser panel (left side, up)
Layers panel (left side, down)




Creating a project
Press “Project” – “New” or Ctrl+N. Save project to the location where your data are stored.


Add layers to project
Layers may be added by:

Drag&drop from Browser panel.
Drag&drop from Windows Explorer / Finder.
Via Data source manager toolbar.




Manage vector layer symbology
Symbology is set to a layer. To access symbology settings, double click a layer in a “Layers” panel (or press right mouse button and select “Properties”), then find and click “Symbology” on the left side of the Properties window.

You can choose one of the default symbols or create your own by customizing fill, outline and other properties.
The layer symbol could itself consist of multiple layers. To add a symbol layer, press “+” button at the upper-left corner.
By default, all features in the layer are painted in a same symbols. You can also change symbol behaviour to “Categorized”, “Graduated”, and other variants.




Manage labels
Labels are usually generated from feature attributes. To access labels settings, double click a layer in a “Layers” panel (or press right mouse button and select “Properties”), then find and click “Labels” on the left side of the Properties window. Change default setting (“No labels”) to “Single labels” to enable label generation




Change map projection
To change map projection, press CRS button at the lower-right corner of the screen. Alternatively, go to “Project” — “Properties” — “CRS”.


This interface allows you to select any of the pre-defined CRS. You can also define your own CRS.
To define your own CRS, choose “Settings” - “Custom projection…”

In the “User defined CRS” window, create a new row, enter the name for your CRS and paste the definition in the desired format (WKT or PROJ).

Note that changing project CRS does not affect layers’ CRS! QGIS performs ‘on-the-fly’ transformation when displaying layers in different projections.
Map window with changed projection will look as follows:



Print layouts
QGIS project supports multiple map layouts.
To create a print layout, navigate to “Project” – “New print layout” or press Ctrl+P. A small prompt window will appear, enter your layout name here. A new print layout will be opened in a separate window.

To add new elements on layout, move elements and element contents, use toolbox on the left.

Most of the elements’ settings are available from the “Item Properties” panel.
Important settings for map are:

lock layers;
grids (allows to draw geographical or projected grid);
size and position.

Map layout may be exported to PNG image, SVG or PDF.
If you have created multiple layouts, they are available from main QGIS window (“Project” – “Layout manager”). Each layout opens in a separate window.


Manage raster layer symbology
Raster layer symbology is different from vector symbology. It is also accessible via “Properties” window. Default setting is ‘Singleband gray’, other available variants are ‘Singleband pseudocolor’, ‘Hillshade’ and others.

title: QGIS Course for NENU students
text:
Welcome to the main page of the QGIS practical course.
This course is designed for trainee students from NENU.
Please note that the exercises in the course do not imply step-by-step instructions. Instead, only key operations and essential screenshots are provided for each task.
The full list of exercises will be provided in the left-hand section of this page. To get started, click on the exercise link.

title: Exercise 2. Raster georeferencing
text:
Objectives

Raster reference interface;
Control points from map;
Key in coordinates of control points;
Raster georeferencing properties



Key steps

Installing plugins;
Georeferencing raster to existing map;
Georeferencing raster with direct coordinate key-in;
Freehand raster referencing in QGIS.



Input data for training


Screenshots and additional information

Install plugins
To install plugins, navigate to “Plugins” — “Manage and Install Plugins…”. You need Internet connection to install plugins from QGIS repository.


Find required plugin in the list of plugins, or start entering its name in “Search…” field at the top of ‘Plugins’ window.
We need a plugin which is called NextGIS QuickMapServices. It allows you to add some publicly available web maps into the project. A few new toolbars or panels can appear in QGIS after the installation. You may close them; turn them on when they are needed.


Add web map to QGIS
To add a map, navigate to “Web” — “QuickMapServices” and select a source to add.

Web maps are not stored locally, you need an Internet connection for proper work.


Raster Georeferencing
Raster (and vector) georeferencing is located in “Layer” — “Georeferencer”


Add a raster to georeference via drag-n-drop or via Open Raster button

Click on raster in Georeferencer window to add a new ground contol point (GCP). You can enter coordinates manually or pick them from map canvas (From Map Canvas button).

Note that coordinates are entered with its CRS. You can then modify target CRS for referencing, and target coordinate number will be recalculated accordingly.
At a first attempt, there will be long red lines indicating error. Ingore them until you set a proper transformation.

Add as many GPSs as needed, click on Transformation Settings button and open settings window. Select proper transformation type and resampling method (not those which are shown below!).

After applying settings, red lines should become relatively small. Check if there are still some errors, correct or remove erroneous points.
When all point setting job is done, press Start Georeferencing button. A new georeferenced file will be created.
